result.title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models
result.comment: 18 pages, 6 figures, 19 tables. Main text and appendices
result.summary: Preference optimization (PO) is the standard way to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models. We find that four public PO checkpoints of LLaVA-1.5-7B also lower object coverage. They name fewer object categories, and their lower hallucination rates bring no significant gain in set-level object F1 on CHAIR. We therefore ask how much of the PO gain the base model can reproduce by stopping earlier. A positive end-of-sequence (EOS) logit bias lets the base model reach the recall of each PO model, and this early stopping alone reproduces 58 to 86 percent of the CHAIRi gain of three checkpoints on two disjoint COCO sets. Writing longer does not bring the lost categories back. Under greedy decoding, a negative EOS bias recovers only 2 to 9 percent of the lost CHAIR recall of these checkpoints, and 94 to 96 percent of the added object mentions repeat categories already named. On CHAIR, the base caption of the same image still names about half of the missed object categories. We therefore propose base-guided object-category restoration, which appends high-confidence base-only categories to the PO caption without training. With thresholds fixed on a development set, it brings three checkpoints within one point of the base recall on a held-out COCO set with a lower distinct-object hallucination rate than the base model. Against the recall-matched base stopping curve, its gain holds for RLAIF-V near the base recall and for RLAIF-V and CHAIR-DPO at an intermediate recall. We will release the code of the recall-controlled evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断 LLaVA-1.5-7B 四个偏好优化检查点在降低物体幻觉的同时压低了物体类别覆盖率，用 EOS logit 偏置模拟提前停止来量化早停可复现多少 PO 增益，并提出免训练、以 base caption 补回高置信类别的恢复方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 与「视觉细节是否被保留并进入输出」以及 STOP 停止决策和覆盖之间的权衡直接相关；其召回受控评价与 base-only 类别筛选可供核查，但讨论对象是 caption 输出而非 latent 推理状态。
